question: A parents' newsletter ran this pie of the apps American teenagers use. YouTube gets under a third. Where's the trick?
answer: In the slices, which add up to 315%. Pew asked 1,316 teenagers which apps they used, and most named several, so each share stands alone: 95% use YouTube, nearly every teenager. A pie works only when each person sits in exactly one slice, as in a vote or a household budget.
move: Before reading a pie, add up its slices; they must make 100.
ask: When I see survey percentages, do I check whether people could give more than one answer?

scene.headline: The apps US teenagers use
scene.label: US teens, 13 to 17, using each
scene.found: Yes: the slices add up to 315%. Teens could pick several apps.
scene.miss: That part is fair. Add up the numbers on the slices.

misses.headline: A plain title. It's the drawing that makes the claim.
misses.label: A fair question. But how many apps could each teen name?

scene.name: A pie past 100%
scene.lesson: A pie is one whole. If its slices add up past 100%, read each one out of 100 instead.

source: Pew Research Center, teens and social media, 2022
reference: Vogels, Gelles-Watnick & Massarat, Teens, Social Media and Technology 2022, Pew Research Center, 10 August 2022
